intent: Test whether maximum forward look-ahead (y=0.08 m) plus a wider seven-sensor array (±0.054 m, 18 mm pitch, 16 mm footprint) reduces line loss and max_error on the s-bend and slalom compared with iteration 2. Drivetrain is unchanged from iteration 2, so the sensor geometry is the only variable being tested.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Moving sensors from y=0.07 to y=0.08 m further reduces max_error on s-bend and slalom, because the controller sees bends earlier. (2) Seven sensors at ±0.054 m keep tape visible to about 0.0745 m offset, which should cut line-loss events on the outer bends. (3) Oval finish rate should stay at or above 65%. If steering_oscillation rises sharply, the extra look-ahead is overshooting, so the next step is a shorter forward offset (about 0.06 m) with the same spread. If max_error still reaches 0.06 m with few line losses, the limit is actuator lag, so the next step is a change in wheel_track or mass rather than more sensing.
rationale: Iteration 2 is the only design that improved on the baseline. Moving the sensors forward to y=0.07 m and using the 16 mm footprint lifted the score from 128 to 329. The oval finish rate rose from 5% to 65%, and s-bend and slalom max_error stayed near the 0.06 m off-track limit. Sensor look-ahead is the lever that has paid off so far. Widening the spread alone (iteration 1) did not help. The outer sensors at ±0.036 m with a 16 mm footprint still lose the tape beyond about 0.0565 m offset, so the controller is blind just before the robot leaves the track. This iteration makes two geometry changes, both aimed at the same failure: (1) move the sensors to y=0.08 m, the forward limit, for maximum look-ahead; (2) use seven sensors at 0.018 m pitch spanning ±0.054 m. Each outer sensor then keeps seeing tape to about 0.0745 m offset, which is beyond the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the robot should not go blind on the bends. I keep the iteration 2 drivetrain (track 0.10 m, radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg) so the comparison isolates the sensor geometry. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and lower max_error on s-bend and slalom versus iteration 2, with oval finish rate held at or above 65%. I expect the s-bend progress to rise above 0.45. This is a hypothesis about sensing; if the Integrator finds the extra sensors add oscillation, the next step is to keep seven sensors and reduce the forward offset.
